The equality assert uses `\g<0>` on the right side, but `\g<0>` refers to the entire match of the left pattern's regex against a name, not a captured group usable for cross-referencing to `ft1`/`ft2` tensor names in this engine's structured-reference syntax—this pattern is not a valid tensor-reference substitution and will not correctly pair each base tensor with its counterpart in ft1/ft2, so the step-1 verification (spec Required result #1) is unlikely to execute as intended. Additionally, the negative lookahead `(?!...)` groups inside the alternation are unnamed but nested, so `\1`-style back-reference logic elsewhere assumes group numbering consistent with the capturing groups later used in `copy`/`add_` transforms, risking group-index mismatches between the exclusion regex and the merge regexes. There is no check that ft1 and ft2 share the same tensor *names* as base (only counts of 244 each), so a corrupted/renamed-tensor case satisfying spec clause "verify that the three checkpoints have the same tensor names" is not actually enforced.
